chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abi Basir, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"When you stand at Arafat, draw near to the hills." [And the hills are the mountains.] "For the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'Those who stand at Arak have no Hajj.'" [Meaning those who stand at the Arak (low ground).]

key_terms.الْأَرَاكِ: The low ground or valley area of Arafat
key_terms.الْهَضَبَاتِ: The hills or elevated ground near Arafat
key_terms.عَرَفَاتٍ: Arafat, the plain where the central ritual of Hajj takes place
key_terms.لَا حَجَّ لَهُمْ: They have no Hajj (indicating deficiency or invalidity depending on interpretation)

ai.seo_question: Where should a pilgrim stand during Wuquf at Arafat according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Abu Abdillah (Imam al-Sadiq) to clarify the preferred topography for the *wuquf* at Arafat, distinguishing between the elevated hills (*al-hadabat*) and the low-lying areas (*al-arak*). While standing in the low ground is often considered sufficient for validity, the Prophet’s statement that 'those who stand at Arak have no Hajj' is interpreted by Shia scholars as indicating a lack of completeness or reward (*naqis al-hajj*) rather than invalidity, emphasizing the Sunnah of following the Prophet’s specific location. This highlights the Shia emphasis on adhering to the precise practices of the Ahl al-Bayt in ritual acts to ensure the Hajj is both valid and perfect.
